question: Does the Pyth price (the settlement source) add information beyond the Kalshi mid, and enough to pay a taker after fees, spread, slippage and latency?
settlement: YES iff the Pyth 1-minute candle close at window close, rounded to the series tick, >= floor_strike (ties YES)
read_before_freeze: Tie rates on the exploration half and liquidity of the last 96 markets (thin-series scan, 2026-10-23). Strike decimals, open/close times and counts (no outcomes). No Pyth price has been seen. On train only: synthetic-bar controls, and gold_proxy.py (Coinbase PAXG-USD as a stand-in, fit on the first half of gold train, read on the second): information gain +0.0054 (CI -0.0004 to +0.0111), taker +3.4c per contract over 834 trades (CI +0.6 to +6.1), +0.4c under latency_60s, +1.5c under stale 60 s. These rules were written before that run and were not changed after it.
periods: train = close <= exploration_end_utc; valid = (exploration_end_utc, valid_end_utc]; test = (valid_end_utc, test_end_utc]; testB = markets opening on or after 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z (prospective). Boundaries are fixed in coverage.json so a later download cannot move them.
alignment_guard: Pyth bars are aligned by the offset (0, -60 or +60 s) at which Pyth at open equals floor_strike for >= 99% of markets with a bar; refuse to run otherwise

signal.pyth: last Pyth 1-minute close at or before T (forward-filled, as Kalshi settles on the most recent data)
signal.sigma: realized from 1-minute log changes over the 3600 s ending at T, per second; needs >= 30 real bars in that hour
signal.skip: no Pyth bar yet, sigma missing or zero, or the Pyth price unchanged for the last 10 minutes (feed closed or stale)

book: bid and ask close of the Kalshi minute ending at T; need 0 < bid < ask < 1 and spread <= 0.05

information_test.fit: train only, one fit per checkpoint: M0 logit(y) ~ logit(mid); M1 logit(y) ~ logit(mid) + (logit(q) - logit(mid)), q clipped to [0.01, 0.99]
information_test.metric: log-loss of M0 minus log-loss of M1 per market-checkpoint, mean with 95% CI clustered by close time

taker.decision: at the first checkpoint where p - (ask + 0.01) - fee > 0.01 buy YES, or (1 - p) - (1 - bid + 0.01) - fee > 0.01 buy NO; one trade per market
taker.price: ask (YES) or 1 - bid (NO) at T + 0.01 slippage

stress.latency_60s: same decision, pay the book of the minute ending at T + 60 s + 0.01
stress.stale_pyth_60s: decide on Pyth and sigma from T - 60 s (seconds left + 60), book at T
stress.slippage_2c: 0.02 instead of 0.01 slippage, in both the decision and the price

maker.decision: at the first checkpoint where p - bid > 0.02 (YES) or (1 - p) - (1 - ask) > 0.02 (NO), join the best bid on that side
maker.fill: a later trade strictly through our price before the end of minute 14

uncertainty: 95% bootstrap CI resampling whole settlement times (2000 draws, seed 1)
pass: Information: valid mean gain > 0 and test CI above 0. Taker: valid mean net > 0; test mean net per contract > 0 with CI above 0 and >= 300 trades; test mean > 0 under latency_60s and stale_pyth_60s; at least 2 of 4 series positive on test. A pass goes to paper trading on testB first. A fail ends E3: no re-tuning on these periods.
gold_proxy_holdout: Only if Cole approves spending gold's valid/test on a stand-in: the same rules on KXGOLD15M with Pyth replaced by floor_strike * PAXG(T) / PAXG(open) (Coinbase PAXG-USD 1-minute closes), fit on all of gold train, read valid once, then test once. Pass as above without the 2-of-4-series clause. If run, gold becomes secondary in E3 and E3's pass needs 2 of the other 3 series.
bankroll_note: At $25 and 1% per position the paper account can only buy contracts costing <= $0.25 with fee; results report that subset too, it does not change the pass rule.
disclosure: fair_value on BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP with Coinbase spot (a proxy, 60 s average settlement) failed on history (edge-audit 2026-10-23). This design reuses E1's blend test and the metals/FX fill rules. Nothing in it was tuned on any Pyth price.
